title: Multi-interface output guarantees PRD and launch checklist for hosted endpoints
creator: Evan Chen
description:
Purpose: Define behavioral contracts and acceptance criteria for the hosted generation surfaces (chat, completions), similarity/embeddings, and rerank endpoints; produce an operational launch checklist and risk mitigations.

Background: Customers rely on predictable latency and consistent quality across our hosted lanes. Existing PRDs focused on surface parity; this document codifies end-to-end guarantees (latency SLO buckets, determinism levels, quality tiers) and the per-endpoint launch steps needed to validate those guarantees in production.

Scope (in-scope): chat/completions API behavior contracts (seed determinism, sampling defaults, tokenization compatibility), embeddings similarity stability and versioning rules, rerank endpoint input/output contracts, SLA and latency SLO definitions by lane, telemetry and eval harnesses for quality regression detection, rollout safety gates and fallback mappings to compatible models.

Out of scope: UI console features, Dedicated/Private-specific deployment automation, storage-level encryption configuration (handled by security infra project), per-customer custom model onboarding flows.

Success metrics: 95th percentile latency within SLO for each lane under target load (see acceptance criteria), zero critical behavior regressions in eval suite for three consecutive nightly runs, rollout automation triggers successfully exercised in staging, and customer-facing SLA language approved by Legal and Product.

Operational assumptions: KV prefix caching and default batching profiles will be enabled for generation lanes in hosted. Smart routing may redirect traffic to compatible model variants if a lane exceeds capacity; fallbacks must preserve behavioral contracts defined below.
acceptance_criteria: Chat baseline: under baseline traffic profile (1k rps simulated with production token distribution) p95 latency <= 220ms for short-turn (~64 tokens) requests and p95 <= 450ms for long-turn (~512 tokens) requests.

Completion parity: completions endpoint returns identical canonical JSON schema and status codes as the spec; sampling defaults aligned with SDKs; stable tokenization compat between model versions (no >1% increase in avg token length).

Embeddings stability: embedding vector dimensionality and similarity distance normalization documented; embedding upgrade path includes automatic re-ranking rollback if top-5 retrieval precision drops >4% vs baseline eval set.

Rerank contract: rerank accepts batched lists of up to 128 candidates; returns stable score ordering and includes per-item confidence; end-to-end rerank latency p95 <= 180ms under admission control threshold.
Determinism tiers: deterministic lanes (for seeding and reproducible evals) document API flags and return deterministic IDs; stochastic lanes default to temperature=0.7 and are labeled in telemetry.
Behavioral regressions: nightly eval pipeline must report no critical regressions for 3 consecutive runs before broad rollout; failing evals block canary promotion.
Telemetry coverage: token-level cost, model variant, routing decision, and KV cache hit/miss counters present for each request and surfaced in per-route dashboards.
Rollout safety gates: canary slice 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on either latency SLO breach or eval regression; canary can be manually aborted by PM/Eng owners.
Docs & SDKs: public API reference updated, guidance on determinism flags and quality tiers added to quickstarts, and at least one SDK patch released that surfaces new default behavior flags.
Legal & Security signoff: SLO wording and product behavior acknowledged by Legal; security review completed with KMS/HSM integration plan attached.
Load & chaos: system sustains target failure scenarios (region failover, model variant OOM) per the runbook with no customer-facing 500s beyond allowable error budget.
launch_checklist: Finalize PRD and circulate to stakeholders (Eng, Design, Security, Legal, Ops, Solutions) - DONE
Lock sampling and determinism defaults in API spec and SDKs - must ship SDK patch
Implement and validate telemetry events (model_variant, route, cache_hit, token_count) in staging and production canary
Create eval suites: quality probes per lane (generation, n-gram overlap checks, embedding precision, rerank ordering tests)
Run 3-night eval stability window and fix regressions before broader rollout
Define SLO dashboards and alert thresholds in Observe; create PagerDuty runbook snippets
Prepare fallback mapping table: lane -> compatible model variant and compatible parameter translation rules
Complete security review and attach KMS/HSM integration checklist
Legal signoff on SLA text and marketplace listings
Conduct cross-team dry run of rollback and canary promotion steps
Open customer communication draft (status page template, developer migration notes)
Create GH PRs linking spec, SDK, and runtime changes; ensure tests pass and have >=2 approvers
Schedule and execute canary rollout (0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) and collect metrics at each step
Post-launch: 72-hour high-touch observability window with on-call Eng and PM monitoring metrics and queued issues triaged every 4 hours
scope_changes: 2026-01-25: Clarified deterministic lanes are opt-in via 'deterministic=true' query flag instead of default; reduces perf overhead by default for stochastic workloads.
2026-02-08: Narrowed embedding upgrade automatic reindexing to run as a staged background job rather than immediate blocking migration to avoid customer disruption.
2026-02-28: Deferred per-tenant custom model onboarding to Private/Dedicated roadmap; Hosted will support only Redwood-curated model variants at GA.
2026-03-03: Increased canary slice progression time windows from 1 hour to 6 hours to allow a more robust statistical signal for small regressions.
